utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness. Witness, would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you state your name.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Namik Dzankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us your date of birth and your age.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of October, 1959. I am 45 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few leading questions to quickly go through some background, and then we'll get right into your evidence. You currently live in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're an economist by trade?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You hold a bachelors and a masters degree in economics.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated at the Faculty for Economics in Sarajevo, and I got my masters degree in Italy in Turin. However, the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina is such that my diploma has still not been accepted in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the masters degree from Turin you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you served in the army from April 1992 through August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in February of 1993, you were named a security operative for the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what is an operative, a security operative?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: A security operative is a soldier working out in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as part of becoming a security operative, since you've been a -- an economist in your career, what special training did you receive?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't receive any special training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about in the area of report writing?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, when I started to work at the security administration, the tasks of interviewing people, gathering data, and making official notes were something that I did with my more senior colleagues and in the process of work I was learning the job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any training in crime scene investigation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any training in the area of investigative techniques?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about training in the area of evidence collection?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any training in the area of security of civilian populations?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, did you have any investigative experience?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: If you're thinking of interviews and evidence collection through such interviews, that is what I did. As for the rest, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then prior to being a security operative, did you have any investigative experience?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And basically before and after the war, you worked as an economist.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to August or the end of August of 1993. Could you tell us where you were.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The end of August?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just before you got to Jablanica, where were you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any notice while you were in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I received an order to report to Jablanica as a member of the coordination and inspection team of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that order, did they say who the chief of the inspection team was?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the chief of the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: General Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were you to report to on the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I was there, I didn't submit one single report to the inspection team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, what I was looking for -- or my question was: Upon arrival, who did you report to on the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I reported to Donja Jablanica -- actually, I arrived at Donja Jablanica, where Mr. Halilovic was and the members of the inspection team. So I reported to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how did you get from Mostar to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you arrive in Donja Jablanica, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was night, around 9.00 or 10.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go upon arriving in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the base at Donja Jablanica. It was the base of Zulfikar Alispago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once you got there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived at the base. I asked whether the members of the inspection team were there. I was told that they were. They were in the room next to the room where I came. I knocked, opened the door, went inside, and said that I was reporting in -- according to orders of the security administration, Mr. Jusuf Jasarevic, as a member of the team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was present when you arrived? Who was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Zulfikar Alispago was there, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, Mr. Vehbija Karic, Zicro Suljevic, and Mr. Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you attend -- what were they -- first, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: They were just sitting and talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sit and talk with them? Did you stay very long? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, I went to Jablanica, where I found accommodation at the Hotel Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe the hotel for us.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What -- what do you mean, "could I describe it"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a small hotel, a large hotel, a lot of rooms, a few rooms?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a large hotel with a lot of rooms. It has three floors with long corridors. And there are rooms on both sides of the corridor. There were a lot of rooms. I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was staying at that hotel?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The clients were mixed. How shall I put it? There were actually refugee there is who had come to Jablanica at the beginning of the war, so they stayed there. They were living there. Then there were members of the army. And there was also a lot of the hospital personnel from Jablanica. These were doctors and medical staff who were not actually from Jablanica. They were refugees who came to Jablanica at the start of the war. They had left their own homeland because of the onslaught of the Chetniks and then because they were doctors and medical staff, they were providing their services to the hospital which was suffering from a shortage of medical staff at the time. So they were living at the hotel and working at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned there were refugees in the hotel. Were there any refugees in the town of Jablanica too?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were refugees in town, and at the time there was also a large number of camp inmates who had been released from Dretelj, Heliodrom, and so on and so forth. So at the time, there was a large number of people in Jablanica, both refugees and camp inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just describe how the refugees who just got out of the camps looked.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: They were hungry. They looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you spend the night there, at that hotel?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next morning. Could you tell us what you did the next morning.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The next morning I went to the directorate of the Jablanica power station, as I had been told. The power station, actually -- administration was across the road. That's where the premises were which were allocated for the inspection team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was there a forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: An official IKM was not formed. There wasn't any such order. But we did call that place the forward command post. Actually, that was the practice in the army. In the brigades and in smaller units, wherever there was a place where there was several officers, whether from the brigade or from the General Staff, that would be called the IKM of the brigade or the IKM of the General Staff. That's how we referred to it. But I didn't see any official order designating that as a forward command post, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a location that you and the others referred to as the forward command post" in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We referred to that place as the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the administrative offices of the hydroelectric plant?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went to this forward command post, which was located across the street from the hotel, who was there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Vehbija Karic, Zicro Suljevic, and Mr. Bilajac, Rifat Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was their positions? Were you on the same level as them? Were they higher than you? Were they lower than you in the military structure?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: They were at more senior positions. I was just a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing at this forward command post?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, they were sitting and talking. There was some papers in front of them. I greeted them. And then they told me that basically an action was being prepared to lift the encirclement of Mostar, to deblock Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what kind of papers that they were working on?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they tell you what the inspection team would be doing?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you what role you had in this operation to deblock Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that I would be doing counter-intelligence work, to walk around town a little bit, to gauge the mood there. Something like that. I didn't actually receive any specific task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, other than the counter-intelligence services that you were to perform, were you given any other duties for the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the operation to deblock Mostar, were you told of any other function or responsibility of the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to inspect or review any soldiers or units?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told anything about the military operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing specific, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you shown any maps of the operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you advised of the name of this upcoming operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn the name of the operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when I came to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you learn it in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When the Trebevic I operation was being conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever advised as to the units that were -- that would be involved, or at that time were you advised as -- as to the units that would be involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that some units from Sarajevo would come, but I didn't know exactly which ones. There was talk that it would be parts of the 9th and 10th, and then later I saw that the 2nd Independent Sarajevo Battalion had arrived as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told where the soldiers that would be arriving would be billeted?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told or advised as to the areas where combat would occur?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was nothing specific said about that, but basically it was known that we would be going to the area of Vrdi, towards Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do over the next few days?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly I was walking around Jablanica. That's when I met Mr. Sejo Brankovic, who was from the Mostar state security, and he took me around Jablanica, and that's how I met the chief of the MUP, Mr. Emin Zebic and his deputy, Salihamidzic. That's when I also met the security officer of the Jablanica Brigade. I don't know his name know, because I didn't spend all that much time with him. And I also met the brigade commander, Kovacevic. He was the commander of the Jablanica Brigade. I walked around Jablanica. Nothing specific. Later, one day with the general and the other team members, we went to Buturovic Polje, to the unit -- actually, to the command of the unit that was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said "with the general." Which general?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic and the other members of the inspection team, meaning Vehbija Karic, Bilajac, and Zicro Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do in -- in Buturovic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing special. I don't mean nothing. We arrived with a view to talking with the command of that unit so that they would give us support in the forthcoming combat operations, if needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I was outside. I walked round the lake with some soldiers and the escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue to stay in that portion of early September. Did you visit the forward command post at all, other than that first day or the day after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you visit the forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As a rule, I went there every day, if I found the gentlemen who were in the inspection team with me there. But very often they were out doing reconnaissance and planning the operations, so that sometimes I would not find them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you attend any meetings in relation to the military operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Throughout this time, I attended only one meeting, when logistical support was discussed, that is, the food needed for the soldiers who had arrived from Sarajevo. I did not attend any other meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was at that meeting and how long did that last?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vehbija Karic, Zicro Suljevic, Rifat Bilajac, the minister, Mr. -- the Minister of the Interior. His name escapes me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Bakir Alispahic, yes. Yes. Yes. Thank you. Yes. And then there was Mr. Kovacevic, the brigade commander, and the mayor of Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any agreements reached as to the food for the troops?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As a rule, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about what day that occurred?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the day when the troops arrived in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that the troops had arrived in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, Mr. Vehbija Karic told me - not me, but all of us - that the troops had arrived and that in the afternoon we should go and visit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit them in Jablanica -- in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us about that, please.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: After the meeting, which lasted for about an hour or an hour and a half, Mr. Karic said that the troops had arrived and that we should go and visit them. We organised ourselves so that we got into two vehicles. The driver of one was the son of Vehbija Karic, and the driver of the other one was a gentleman whom I only know by nickname. His nickname was Soko. We got into those cars. It was around lunchtime, and we went to Donja Jablanica, to Zuka's base, where I personally loaded three or four tins with food packed inside. There were pies inside, to take them to the soldiers and give this to them to eat, because they had been on the road from Sarajevo throughout the night and a good part of the day over Mount Igman and through Buturovic Polje, as far as Jablanica. So we took this food to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Jablanica, what units were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to Jablanica or Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's Monday morning. Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Grabovica, there were parts of the 9th and 10th Brigade there and parts of the Independent Battalion, and the commander of that battalion was Adnan Solakovic. The name of that unit was the 1st Independent Sarajevo Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you familiar with people or the reputations of these three units?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I personally knew only two men, who were friends of mine and who I grew up together in Vogosce. They were members of the 1st Independent Battalion. As for the others, I didn't know them personally. And what do you mean by "reputation"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the common knowledge and what was being said in Sarajevo, where you worked and where you lived most of your life. What was the reputation or the view -- let's start off with the 10th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. As regards the 9th and the 10th Brigades, I have to say that these were units which had exceptionally good fighters and which held the most inaccessible and worst parts of the battlefield in Sarajevo and they saved that town. Also, small parts of those units were outside control. I can't speak about the 9th and 10th Brigade because the brigades as a whole did not have a bad reputation. It was only parts of those units that had a bad reputation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The parts of the units that had the bad reputation, what did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. The biggest problem was that they took civilians to dig trenches. That was a problem I knew about, that people in town talked about. I don't know about any other problems there were. Possibly there was an incident, that is, when members of the 9th disarmed and maltreated members of the security administration. I forgot to mention that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you said "civilians were taken to dig trenches," were these people going voluntarily, these civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't do it voluntarily. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they find these civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- did this include people of all occupations?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the residents go into the -- did the residents of Sarajevo go into the areas where these units would be staying as a result of this?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. Those who didn't have to go there avoided going there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you -- let's return to Grabovica. You see these soldiers from these three units there. Were you involved in the billeting of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you involved in the billeting of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was involved in housing or billeting or accommodating these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to perform a security analysis of billeting soldiers in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the danger of billeting soldiers with civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. It presumes that there was a danger of billeting soldiers with civilians. That's the thing the Prosecutor is trying to prove in this case. He's not to ask a leading question about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us whether there is a danger of billeting soldiers with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, again, I object. That has to be made clear, whether this is an abstract question in principle or whether it relates to that particular episode.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a general question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe it's a general question, you know. You may proceed, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question was: Could you tell us whether there is a danger in billeting soldiers with civilians.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not an expert in these matters. I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have billeted the soldiers of the 9th and 10th Brigade with civilians in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. Firstly, it's speculative. And secondly, there's been a clear answer in the previous question that's asked that he's not an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has already answered that question. There's no need to repeat this question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, one was a general question. The other one is a specific question in relation to Grabovica, where he was with those soldiers who he's just testified were -- that had -- were from units that had minorities that were out of control and did not treat civilians well in Sarajevo. I think he could answer that particular question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no difference between the two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Grabovica, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I got to Grabovica, I distributed the food to the men who were there. They were around the houses, lying down on the grass, resting. And wherever I saw a relatively large group of soldiers, I brought the food containers with the food to the soldiers so that they could have lunch. I took the last food container to Adnan Solakovic's unit, that is, the 1st Sarajevo Battalion, in order to look for these two friends I had there, Zoran Kovacevic and Cupo. I don't know what his name is because we all called him Cupo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find these friends?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you spend any time with them?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The whole time we were there I spent with them. I found Cupo, who was in the first building - the first house on the right-hand side; it's a damaged building - and he said that Zoran Kovacevic was in the house above that and that he was sleeping. I went up there and woke him up. We came back and we ate together and we talked. I was interested in finding out what was going on in Sarajevo because I hadn't been there for a long time. I wanted to know if any friends or neighbours had been killed, and things like that. So that's what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, may the witness be shown exhibit or photograph P7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the photograph in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, do you recognise that area?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the usher please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you recognise this area, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise that as?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the village of Grabovica and the area where the soldiers were billeted. Well, they weren't exactly accommodated there. They were just scattered around. At the time, we didn't know who was in what house. There had not been a roster yet -- drawn up yet or a disposition of the men arranged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the area where you sat and spoke with your friends depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using that --

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: It's the ruined building on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you sit and speak with your friends by that ruined building?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Throughout the time we were there, which was about an hour or an hour and a half. Throughout this time, I sat there and talked to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please put a circle identifying the area where you sat and spoke with your friends.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were there, where was Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: They walked around from group to group and talked to the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, were there any line-ups of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any calls for line-ups of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Karic, Suljevic, or Bilajac with any soldiers in a line-up?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that one to one-and-a-half hour period, did you see any military police in the area?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: None of the men wore military police insignia. In that entire village, none of the men actually had any insignia, either of a brigade or anything else, and I did not see any military police insignia on any of the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were there during this hour and a half, you sat and spoke with friends and ate. Others were eating. What were some of the other soldiers doing who weren't eating?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. There were men there who were sleeping on the grass. Across the way, in this big house here, when I passed by, there was a lady standing on the steps. And as I was passing by carrying the food container, I greeted her and I said to her, "Madam, are these men of ours obedient?" And she said, "Oh, yes, they're wonderful. They're chopping wood for me and I'm baking a pie for them." There was another elderly man in front of the house who was showing a man which figs were ripe and which figs he could pick and which ones he shouldn't pick.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- may we offer that photograph at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P280.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after about an hour to an hour and a half that you stayed there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We got into the vehicles and returned from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go after you left Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in a vehicle with Soko. We went to Jablanica. I got out at the hotel. I went into the hotel. I found Mr. Brankovic. And together we went out for a walk and after that to have dinner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to later on that same evening, between 9.00 and 11.00 p.m. Did something happen?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That night, Mr. Brankovic and I were in my room in the hotel. We were sitting there and talking. And in the corridor of the hotel we heard a rumour, a commotion. He and I went out of the room to see what was going on. In the corridor, there were several men, some in uniform and some not, and they were saying that in Grabovica civilians had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after you heard that the civilians had been killed in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brankovic and I went back into our rooms, got dressed, and then went outside the hotel, where there were quite a few civilians gathered, and people were commenting on the news. People had heard the news. Mr. Brankovic and I then went to the public security station in Jablanica to see Mr. Zebic and Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the second name? You saw Mr. Zebic and Mr. ...?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First let's talk about outside the hotel. When you went outside the hotel you saw many people out there. Were there people in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, no. There were some people in uniforms, but most of them were civilians; although, in our parts many members of the army did not have uniforms, so I can't say exactly who were soldiers and who were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the discussion outside?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The discussion was about this event, that members of units from Sarajevo had killed civilians in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from here we're going -- where did you go from here? You said you went to the police station in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're going to be discussing a number of meetings and conversations you had over the next several days. Did you have a diary with you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you maintain any records of the meetings and indicating the dates that you met and spoke with people?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. At that time, I had a small notebook in which I noted down some things. But later I used that to write reports. And after I had done that, I destroyed my notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any sort of datebook listing the dates of these various meetings?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As I told you, it was a small diary in which I noted down not just the dates but some notes that I felt I would need. But later on, when I had drawn up an official report, I would destroy the notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you went to the MUP in Jablanica and you said you met with Emin Zebic and Ahmed Salihamidzic. Did you have any discussion with them?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Our aim was to find out whether they had heard about the events in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the rest of the discussion?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed how we could gather as much information as possible, see what had actually happened, and what we should do about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any further discussion?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you do next? Or what do you recall that you do next?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We agreed that I, Mr. Salihamidzic, and Brankovic should go to see Mr. Zulfikar Alispago, Zuka, that we should go to where he was staying, and that was close to the public security station, that we should talk to him and see what he knew about it and whether he could give us more details; in other words, to find out what he knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you wind up going to Zuka's apartment?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when do you believe you went there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Whether it was that same night or the following night, I can't recall exactly, but I know that we did go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to Zuka's apartment, who -- first, who went to Zuka's apartment with you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brankovic and Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was present at Zuka's apartment?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived there, we found Mr. Zuka and Mr. Edib Saric, who was the commander of, I think, Cedo's Wolves. That was the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any discussion at that apartment?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We discussed what had happened in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us specifically what words you recall being discussed.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I can't tell you exactly who said what. I can't recall exactly. But I can tell you the essence of what we said. We discussed what had happened down there. Zuka said that he had found two children whom he had saved, that he had taken them to his unit, and that when he went there he was unable to see everything, and that he came back later on and we talked about it. In the meantime, he -- or rather, Celo, that is, Ramiz Delalic, entered the apartment with Malco, his deputy or -- I don't know whether he was his deputy exactly, but he was with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just before we get to Celo enters, did Zuka discuss the plight of any of his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: His soldiers were in Donja Jablanica. That's a few kilometres from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion of -- about any of his soldiers being killed?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: He said then that because one of his soldiers of Croat ethnicity was missing, he assumed that he was one of them. But because they couldn't find him at that particular point in time, they didn't know whether he had been killed or not, but they assumed that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said at some point Ramiz Delalic, known as Celo, enters. What was his disposition at the time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't in a good mood. He was angry and in a bad mood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say? What do you recall him saying?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When he came in, he immediately told Zuka that he wanted to have vehicles secured because he wanted to return his soldiers to Sarajevo, he didn't need this, he wanted to shoot -- or two of his soldiers, that he didn't want to be there any more, that he wanted to have trucks so that he could return to Sarajevo, to which Zuka replied that he should wait because the action was going to start. "Don't do it because of those people in Mostar. They need help down there." And then Zuka said that he would try to get in touch with Mr. Halilovic, General Halilovic, to consult him, and to ask that he comes to Jablanica as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion of Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was no discussion. Ramiz was outraged with everything that happened and he said something to the effect that Bakir Alispahic and his Lastes should be conducting this war and let them finish this action, something like that. That was what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Celo, or Ramiz Delalic, calm down during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that's a leading question, and you'll recall what the evidence was from the previous witness, was -- which was quite to the contrary of that, so it's particularly objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that, Your Honour. He speaks -- he's mentioning another witness in front of this witness, which is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's inappropriate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, let's stop the argument at this stage. Well, maybe you moved too fast, Mr. Weiner. Could you go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during -- during this meeting -- first, how long did this meeting last at Zuka's house?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: An hour to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was Celo, or Ramiz Delalic, at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: About half an hour. Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay for the whole meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did stay for the whole meeting. Actually, I was there up until the time when Mr. Brankovic and Mr. Salihamidzic and I left the meeting, if we can call it a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left, was Celo's troops staying or leaving for Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The decision was not made, and I could not decide based on that. Zuka was asking him to stay, and he wanted to leave. But there was no definite decision at the time. When we left, they stayed together at that apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We went back to the station -- the public security station in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. We talked about the meeting, and then everyone left. Brankovic and I went back to the hotel. He went back to his room; I went back to my room. We were writing down notes, reports, and so on. What we heard, we were putting down on paper -- actually, that's what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write a report that evening?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not the whole report. I drafted a part of it. I sent the first report immediately after the events. Actually, as soon as I found out about the events, I sent the first report to the security administration of the General Staff, just a couple of sentences stating what happened, in which area, and which units were billeted in that area. I sent that to General Jusuf Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when did you send that? Was that on the same day, the next day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. There is to be no leading in relation to the date of that being sent. The witness can answer the question himself as he -- well, that's the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no problem with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can explain the problem very clearly. My learned friend knows exactly what it is. If he wants to object to me making speeches in front of the witness, then the witness should be given the chance to take a break now and I'll explain what the problem is. But perhaps I can do it simply. If Your Honour refers to the -- to the proofing note and the date that's mentioned of sending that first report on that proofing note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, I believe that is a combined question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could ask the first question first, and then ask the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you send that report?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That night the events happened, the killings. In the morning, I sent the first report. This event, or the killing, happened in the evening. The next morning I sent the first report, which contained about four to five sentences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what exactly, as best as you recall, you said when you sent that report the following morning.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat: I wrote that there was a killing of civilians in the sector of Grabovica by members of the B and H army, parts of the 10th, 9th, and the independent units were in that area, and I said that more information would follow; I would continue to compile data, and as soon as I had some more information, I would pass it on to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you do that day?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said you got up -- or that morning, you sent out a report. Did you see anyone else? Did you speak with anyone else on that date? This is the day after the killings. What do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The day after the killing, in the evening we were in the room, myself and Mr. Brankovic, and somebody knocked on the door, and Mr. Sefer Halilovic -- General Sefer Halilovic was at the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation with Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell the Court what that conversation was.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic came to the door. Mr. Sejo Brankovic and I were there. After we said hello, Mr. Halilovic asked me, "Namik, have you heard about what happened in Grabovica?" And I said I did. Mr. Halilovic told me, "Namik, I am not behind that. I do not justify it. I want you to collect as much information as possible and send it and inform the Sarajevo command about it." I replied that I was already in contact -- or actually, together with Sejo Brankovic, that I had gone to the public security station and that I had already sent a very short initial report to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any further conversation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't really speak about anything more specifically. That was the conversation more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during the day, did you visit the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I tried -- yes. Yes, yes. In the morning, I went to the hydroelectric power plant building, where Mr. Zicro Suljevic, Bilajac, and Vehbija Karic were. This was sometime after breakfast. They were in the big conference room. I went in and said hello to them and asked them if they had heard about the events in Grabovica. They said that they had not, and then I briefly told them what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, not what happened but what I knew at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what conversation did you have with them, if any?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I told them that I had been to the public security station, that I had already sent the first report, and then they said -- actually Vehbija Karic said, "Namik, could you please do your best and continue to collect as much information as you can. Continue to work on it."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the day, where did you go after you spoke with the -- the three generals at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That day, together with Sejo Brankovic, I tried -- actually, we borrowed a vehicle from Mr. Emin Zebic and we tried to go to the Grabovica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before you're trying to go, you said you borrowed a vehicle. Did you have your own vehicle or a military security vehicle while you were in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any communications equipment, you yourself have any communications equipment while you were in Jablanica? Meaning a Motorola or a radio of some kind.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of uniform did you have?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I had a -- a pilot's work suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you have a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: During the four years that I was in the army, I was never issued a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a military security ID?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The IDs were printed in Sarajevo before I left Sarajevo. But since I had left Sarajevo when Igman was falling, when the Chetniks were very close to Sarajevo, within reach of Sarajevo, I went out there to prevent this offensive. I left my ID in Sarajevo because there is a big difference if you are captured as a soldier or if you are captured with an ID of the security administration of the General Staff. Then you would be treated quite differently. So I didn't carry it with me because of my own personal safety, because throughout the time I was always practically walking on the lines of separation or I was at the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to borrow a police vehicle while you were in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zebic gave me a vehicle for my use that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brankovic and I got into the car and tried to go to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "tried to go to Grabovica." Please tell the Court what happened.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We came to Donja Jablanica, just further down from the base of Zulfikar Alispago's unit. That's where the checkpoint was where the soldiers were, and they didn't allow us to pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why couldn't you pass through?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: They said that we couldn't pass because that was a combat operation zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you do?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to the police station, did you have any discussion with anyone there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I returned to the police station, I talked -- well, actually, we would always drop by and speak with Mr. Zebic and Mr. Salihamidzic. We would exchange information, although I was actually the one who profited the most, because I received most of my information from them. These were people who were on their home ground. I could get information from them. They would know the names of those who were killed. I wouldn't be able to know that. So they helped me. As I said, I received most of my information from them. And whatever I found out, I would inform them about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us what happens at the hotel. Now, did anyone offer any assistance to you, anyone from the inspection team, from Mr. Halilovic, to Karic, Suljevic, Bilajac? Did anyone offer any assistance to you on that date, or any date after that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't receive any assistance simply because the gentlemen from the inspection team very quickly after that, that day or the next day, left to go to the combat operation zone for reconnaissance and to plan the operation, so that after those meetings I no longer had the opportunity of meeting with the gentlemen from the inspection team -- the gentlemen from the inspection team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after that date, you never met any of them again?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, had you ever been involved in an investigation of this type?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Had you ever been involved in a case of that type?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been involved in any major criminal investigation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much experience did you have as a criminal investigator?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The small amount of experience that I had before I left Sarajevo working with my senior colleagues, that was basically my experience. That is why later in my report I asked for assistance from Sarajevo, to have police officers sent to me, on-scene crime technicians, an investigative judge to help me with the investigation. This is what I requested from my superiors in Sarajevo, but I never got this assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any training in complex criminal matters or major crimes?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any training in homicide investigation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you weren't able to get to Grabovica on that day. Did you ever go to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you go?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're -- we're not receiving any interpretation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did go. A couple of days after, I borrowed a car again from Mr. Zebic and then went to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you. And thank you for the interpretation. And how were you able to go at that time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I was at the checkpoint, I said that I was going to see Samir Pezo, who is my friend. We grew up together in Velesici. That's what I said. And then they let me pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you see when you got there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I got there, since Adnan Solakovic's unit, or the 1st Sarajevo Battalion, was billeted at the old railway station at the very entrance, that's where I parked my car. I saw Adnan and Samir in front of the building. I came out of the car, greeted them, said hello to them, and then at the side there's a kind of wooden bench and table, and this is where I sat down together with Samir Pezo. And when we were walking towards that bench, we were just talking, and I just asked him, "Samir, what happened exactly?" And he said, "Oh, please, don't ask me anything." "I was on guard duty," he said, "around the building, because I was afraid for my soldiers who are of a different ethnic group." That's when Adnan Solakovic came up to us. He said hello to me, sat down, and when he heard what we were talking about, he said, "Well, just forget about that now. You see what the situation is now, and in any case, combat operations have started." And as we were talking, at that point a jeep arrived from the direction of Jablanica. It stopped. And Ramiz Delalic came out of the jeep, as well as Dzeki. That's, I think, the commander of the Handzar Divizija Unit. Saric came out. Well, there were a couple of these commander there is of these units that were in the process of conducting combat operations. When they came out of the car, they stopped about 10 metres away from us, and at that point in time our guys began to report via the Motorola that they had broken through the lines and that they had taken Mali and Veliki Medvjed. When we heard that, we got up and approached closer to hear what the situation was, how many wounded, how many killed. But actually the mood was quite celebratory because we had broken through the lines. After that, I said goodbye to everyone. I got into the car and returned to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Motorolas. What's a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: A means of communication. A communication device.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who had these Motorolas or radios?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: From what I could see, one was held by Ramiz Delalic. He had it in his hand. And his one was turned on. I think that Dzeki also -- I'm not sure. As far as I can remember, also had one. But the one that Ramiz Delalic had was operating at that time, and that's how we heard what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think now would be a time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to return again to that visit you made to Grabovica where you met Adnan Solakovic and Samir Pezo. Did you make any observations in the area, any observations relating to the massacre?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you left a short time after the -- they received the good news, the soldiers received the good news over the radios. Why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I left because I saw no reason to stay. At that point in time, with regard to the goal of my arrival, there was no one for me to talk to. Both Adnan and Samir were very sparing in their comments. And then when the celebrations started and the rejoicing, then it seemed out of place for me to bring up what had happened before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, I'd like to show you some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit 215, 215.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterdays

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show me the document to the end? I can see almost nothing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the document please be scrolled to the end.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise that document as?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the reports I sent to the military security administration, to the attention of the General Jusuf Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the end, you made five proposals, mainly in relation to the establishment of a investigative team. Why did you make those proposes, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps they should be brought up on the screen so that the Court can see them when the -- when the witness is discussing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's page 3 in the English. In Bosnian, it's page 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you request that a -- an investigative team be formed?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I requested -- I requested it for the simple reason that I alone, as an individual, could do nothing. First of all, because I'm not trained to do that job and I am not an expert on it. And according to what little knowledge I had, and in view of the meagre training I had had, I felt that this case required an investigation conducted by a large number of experts and trained professionals. That's why I asked my superior, General Jusuf Jasarevic, for assistance. I asked that he send me a team which would assist me -- or rather, which -- if such orders were issued, could carry out the investigation, because, let me repeat, I alone as an individual with no command authority and not properly trained for this job, was unable to carry it out. That's why I asked the general for assistance, either that they should assist me or that they should conduct the investigation themselves. However, I never received any assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've testified that you sent an initial report out, a very short report, on September 9th. This report dated September 13th, what report was this? Was this basically the second, the third, the fourth, fifth, sixth? As best as you can recall.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, this was the second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness next be shown Exhibit 225, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the report in front of you, or the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to coming to The Hague, had you ever seen this document before? Or prior to speaking with The Hague investigators.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever received any communication with this information or with making these requests from Chief Jusuf Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you obtained any of this information that was requested by this date, the 15th of September?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I never obtained any of this information, nor did I ever receive any order in connection with these events from the gentlemen in the security administration or the 6th Corps. I see it says here "command of the 6th Corps." They never contacted me in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever file any other reports while you were in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a third report, as far as I can remember, where I collected the names of the victims and some other information I had managed to collect in cooperation with the gentlemen from the Jablanica Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown MFI235, please.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is dated on September 29th. Where were you when you drafted this report?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you send it to?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusuf Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the information as to the names, you indicated you received them from the Jablanica Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next two paragraphs -- or actually, the next paragraph, relating to the Pranjics, where did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In the Jablanica Public Security Station. That's where I got this information. But I'd heard about it before that. I mean, I got the names from the public security station, but before that I had heard that Adnan Solakovic's unit had saved two civilians, and later on I learned their names from the gentlemen in the Jablanica Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the last sentence in this document mentions an on-site investigation and exhumation procedure to be carried out by the MUP and the Jablanica military police. Was there any agreement for those activities to be reached?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: We talked about it in the Jablanica Public Security Station, but there was no agreement, no specific agreement. We did discuss it, however. We discussed that what was possible should be done. We did not, however, reach any specific agreement about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an order ever issued for an on-site investigation or for an exhumation in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the order I received from Mr. Halilovic that night, that I should do everything in my power and inform and collect information, I received no further orders from anyone in connection with this investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Jablanica, was there ever an on-site investigation and an exhumation procedure in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of it. I don't know whether or not anything else was done about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this report on September 29th, did you ever file any other reports in relation to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever request a status report from you in relation to this incident in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: After this, I returned to Sarajevo very quickly, and nobody ever asked me for any kind of report or discussed Grabovica with me in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the inspection team, Mr. Halilovic or any other generals or high-ranking officers, ever speak to you about Grabovica after September 9th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown MFI222. Actually, I think that became Exhibit 222 on Friday, I believe. Could he be shown page 3 of that, the report of Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not page 3. I only have the beginning of the document, the title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. That's the -- there's another document in front of that, sir. So that's the first page of the second document, which begins on page 3 of the exhibit. Could you look at that page 3 and the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think they have the wrong document on the screen. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a frozen computer screen, so we're going to use a paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm happy for the witness to be shown a paper copy. It's sometimes useful because the -- as Your Honour pointed out, the Salihamidzic document is headed "Official note." So that's one way of knowing. The other one -- the Brankovic document, has no such heading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it's a note or a -- an official note compiled by Mr. Ahmed Salihamidzic, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you'll notice that in this document he discusses the various meetings that you and he and others attended, especially on the second page. One paragraph begins on September 10, another one in the morning of September 9th, another one on September 10th.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you notice -- there's actually another one on September 10th. The dates of the meetings that he describes seem to be a day or a few days different from yours. Do you know any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that ought to be -- I suppose -- I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you. The possibility of making a mistake in the dates, well, we all worked -- or rather, speaking for myself, I worked as well as I was able to. Reports were not drawn up and sent on the same day. They took several days to compile. And the possibility of making a mistake in the date was there. At the time, the date didn't mean much to me. My goal was to collect as much information as possible and to inform the command in Sarajevo. Now, 12 years later, I really cannot be 100 per cent certain whether it was the 8th or the 9th or the 10th. The chronology of events, as I have told them, is something I abide by, but now, 12 years later, I cannot guarantee that the dates are all correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown Exhibit 214, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive that document?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever receiving any assistance from the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. I received no assistance and no one ever contacted me. I see that my name is mentioned in this report, and there are some words which I allegedly said, but this is not true. No one ever contacted me, nor did I ever tell anyone that Vehbija Karic or anybody else among the members of the inspection team ordered me to stop the investigation. This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my question, as to whether anyone had ever ordered you to stop. And your response is that it's not correct, that it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No one ever gave me such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown MFI232. Could they turn to the text of the document. The front page is on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen that document prior to being shown -- shown it by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive it at any time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the Uzdol incident during the month of September while you were in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I learned about it when I returned to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever give you any assignments in relation to Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even after you returned to Sarajevo, did you receive any communications or assignments in relation to Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we move to 65 ter document 132, which has an ERN of 0342-9809.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI281.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the book. Your Honours, I object to this. There's a lot that needs to be discussed about this book. Now, I don't know whether to raise an ad hoc objection right now or whether the witness should be given a break and we can raise it properly. But if it's to be shown to the witness now, then I want to raise what I have to raise about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we have some procedural matters to discuss, so Madam Usher will show you out of the room, and after that we'll invite you to come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Let's talk about the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
