utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Well, this book is not an appropriate -- this witness is not an appropriate person to put this book to, in the least. As I understand it, he hadn't seen it until he was generously shown it by the Prosecutor. He hasn't acted on it. It hasn't guided anything he did or influenced any of his recollections in any way. And frankly, it's just a -- got nothing to do with this witness whatsoever. It's just irrelevant to him completely. So for that reason -- well, there's a number of technical sort of objections to raise, but right now there's a very simple one, and that is that this is just an unrelated document to him. So I object to it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, we have to establish that through the questions and the answers. Maybe you could allow the Prosecution to ask some preliminary questions on this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I certainly will, Your Honours. I think I should raise the objection now because I think the Prosecutor has indicated in the proofing note what is the status of this witness is in relation to that. Your Honour is right. Of course there are some preliminary questions to ask, but they're hollow and pointless unless they lead to a particular answer. And I think my friend may know what the answer is already. Anyway, I'll -- that's my objection at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is aware that the -- that this defendant had written a book and that several other generals of various sides during war had written a book about their exploits. What the witness can talk about is there are four different passages where his name is mentioned as to what he was doing, what was said to him, what he in fact said, and he would like to comment on each of those. We would then introduce the book through other witnesses. So basically we would have him comment on those four passages where it mentions he was he was given certain assignments or he had certain conversations with the defendant. And as to the truth or correctfulness of those, and then from there we would introduce the book at some later time through another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that -- that didn't answer the question and the issue in any way, and it leaves also open this question, which Mr. Weiner can now answer, I imagine. Through which witness is he proposing to introduce this book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be at a future time. We'll introduce it. I'm not going to give up any of our strategy or our -- or our plans it to counsel. It's not required and I have no intention of doing it, Your Honour. It will be introduced through another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the -- which witness you are going to use this document, I believe that I have no intention to know at this stage, but I could not agree with you that you could not tell the Defence about your strategy at this stage. Because we have heard about more than half of the witnesses already, and I think you should present your case entirely to this Court and to the Defence, just to avoid any surprise attack on the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We were planning to introduce it through Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Concerning of using this document, I believe that the name of the -- this witness is mentioned. The witness is entitled to comment on those parts of the document, so the Prosecution is allowed to ask some questions on those relevant parts of this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand the ruling. I won't argue with that part of it. But there is another issue as to this. Just because the Prosecutor says he wants to introduce it through another irrelevant witness -- or another witness who has no relationship to this -- to this document, does not mean that he's entitled to show it to this one. Now, my friend has said that he wanted to introduce it through Mr. Hodzic. But that's not good enough, frankly. It has to be shown that Mr. Hodzic would be entitled to have that document put to him, and it would have to be shown that Mr. Hodzic is a witness through whom that document ought to be presented. Your Honours, as you know, past statements of witnesses and in some cases of accused people, can in some circumstances be admitted. And they may have some probative value in certain circumstances. But it is not good enough simply to say, "Well, Mr. Halilovic or his editors at some point compiled a book which at some point may have been published in its original form or a -- or a different form. What has to be shown is that that's his words and that he's acknowledged them. And doing that through this witness or through Mr. Hodzic -- in fact, Your Honours, what I will say is that Mr. Hodzic is a worse person to put it through than this witness. At the moment, I'm very troubled by this. It seems to me -- I'm not attempting to impute bad faith in any way, but it seems to me this is an attempt to get this document in without the usual course that the Prosecutor should follow of calling one of their investigators, which Your Honours have noticed no doubt does not appear on the witness list in this case. Now, if they wanted to say, "Well, as an investigator we've gathered various pieces of information that may be of use to the Court," then in that situation sometimes you might accept that -- that document, that book, or some other thing that Mr. Halilovic might have said on other occasions. But to put it through witnesses who -- to whom it's just a free -- to whom it's got no relationship at all is not proper and not acceptable. Now, Your Honours is in one sense right. If it were acceptable to put it through Mr. Hodzic, if the document were otherwise admissible, frankly, Your Honours' Honour's ruling, if I may say so, is entirely correct of course. Then if the document was going to be -- then I wouldn't have an objection to show that to the document as propose. But what hasn't been established yet is that the document should be put through Mr. Hodzic at all. And it has to be shown that there is some proper basis for that being done. At the moment I'm not aware of any. And that's why I asked the question, frankly, to see who it's going to go through, because we know who's left now in terms of the Grabovica witnesses and it looks to me as if not one of them was a proper one. Now that the name Mr. Hodzic has been mentioned, what I want to submit is that there could be no proper basis. It's not good enough, for example for Mr. Hodzic to have written a book of his own. It's not good enough that Mr. Hodzic may have read part of the book or seen part of the book. That's got knob to do with it. Otherwise, it could have been given to Mr -- Witness D to read in proofing and then put to him. Your Honours, there has to be some sense here to have putting this evidence through a proper witness. Your Honours' ruling is right, but it operates on a basis that the documents otherwise tenderable through Mr. Hodzic. And at the moment the Prosecution hasn't shown in any form why Mr. Hodzic is better off. And it -- what I want to do is to make it clear that it would not be sufficient merely to say Mr. Hodzic has read it, because the Prosecutors have read it as well, but that doesn't -- that doesn't suffice. So that's what I have to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that at this stage we have to distinguish two matters: One is using of this document in the proceedings; the other is admission into the evidence of this document. They are two related but somehow separate matters. I believe this document is published as a book, which is available by everybody, and in this case I don't think there's any problem to admit this document into the evidence at all. But anyway, the Trial Chamber will consider the testimonies of all those witnesses related to this book in the future and then we'll decide whether to admit it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm -- I'm bound by Your Honour's ruling on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So could we call back the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we just discussed some procedural matters, and I apologise to you for the interruption. Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzankovic, do you know whether the defendant, Mr. Halilovic, has written a book?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I found out about it from the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which media in particular? Meaning, was it radio, television, newspapers, magazines? Which media?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I read it in the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you purchase a copy of this book or do you have one?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a passage of it which concerns Uzdol and Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown that passage again. That's 65 ter 132, and that's 0342-9809.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you four different quotations in that. The first one is on page 2 of the English, which is page 114 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have page 114 of the B/C/S in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a page, but I don't see the number. I don't see the page number. I do have the document here though.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It should be the 9810 has the number 114 on the bottom. So it's the second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the middle of that, which is the middle paragraph, sir, in the middle of the middle paragraph it says: "A part of the team (Bilajac, Suljevic, and Karic) went out on 1 September 1993 together with Namik Dzankovic and Hasanpasic to conduct preparations for stationing units in the Jablanica sector as the plan of the operation envisaged their engagement along the village of Vrdi-Listica access." Sir, did that ever occur?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the time, I was actually in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved at all with the stationing of units in the Jablanica sector?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or the preparation for the stationing of units?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we continue on that same page, which would be pages 2 and 3 in the English, at the -- beginning with the last paragraph: "On the morning of 4 September ...." It talks about a meeting of Rasim Delic arriving in Jablanica and that the defendant reported to Rasim Delic, informing him of the details of the operation. And then on the next page, it says: "All the team members, the commander of the 6th Corps, commander of the 46th Brigade, commander of the Zulfikar Reconnaissance and Sabotage Brigade were present at the time." On September 4th, did you ever attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was in Mostar at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us continue. On page 4 in the English, the third paragraph, which is page 117 on the bottom in the B/C/S, which is page 9813 on the top. Do you see that paragraph: "According to the report by a team led by Bilajac, the tragic incident in the village of Grabovica took place on the night between the 7th and 8th of September, 1993. The team learnt about the incident from its member, Namik Dzankovic, an operative in the ARBiH security administration at about 1000 hours on 8 September. According to Jankovic's report, he had learnt about it in the Jablanica SJB public security station. He immediately informed the other organs of the Jablanica SJB, were attempting to shed light on this tragic incident" - I'm sorry - "tragic event. The SVK team ordered him to take part in the work of the MUP, Ministry of the Interior, team to help identify the perpetrator." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I said before, that I came to see the gentlemen at the hydroelectric power plant in Jablanica. I asked them if they knew what had happened. I informed them that I had been at the public security station in Jablanica and that I had sent the first report to Sarajevo, to the security administration. Then I was told what I already said. Mr. Karic said that I should try to find as many -- as much information about it as possible and then -- and that I should work together with the security organs in Jablanica, which is what I did. That is more or less it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then the next paragraph, sir: "On the afternoon of 9 September, I arrived in Jablanica from Konjic and Dobro Polje. Namik immediately told me what happened. I ordered him there and then to inform the security administration and Rasim Delic immediately to seek assistance from the administration, to take part along with security organs of the 44th Jablanica Brigade in the work of the MUP team, and to immediately request that the 6th Corps security chief come over because the tragic incident took place in the zone of responsibility of the 6th Corps. Namik responded by saying that he had already done most of this on his own initiative and that on the basis of his responsibilities as a security organ. He also said that he would try and carry out the rest of the tasks I had given him at the very earliest." Sir, do you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the conversation that I spoke about before, when the general came to my door, to the door of my room in the Jablanica Hotel, and issued an order. This order wasn't as specific as it says here. Before that, he said, "Namik, I am not behind this. I would like to have as much information gathered as possible and the command in Sarajevo informed about it." What it says here as a fact -- actually it's true that I did carry out most of the tasks that are mentioned here later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, were you given those specific orders to carry out those tasks by Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not as specifically as it is stated here, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What orders were you given by Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I am repeating: The general told me, "Namik, I'm not behind this. I do not justify it. I would like to have as much information gathered as possible and that the command in Sarajevo is informed about it or, actually, the security administration," of which I was a member, and this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any other orders by Sefer Halilovic in relation to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I repeat once again: Not from him or from any of the other members of the team, because after that they went to the combat operation zone and I was not able to communicate with them because I did not have any means of communication. So the communication that I actually conducted was one-way communication, in which I was passing on the information I had compiled on to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to show you another document, the last of the documents. It's a Defence document, MFI130. Sir, were you aware -- or first, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, were you aware that a report was filed by the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name mentioned on the first page?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, under number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the last page, there are signatories.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see that. I don't have that page in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the registrar please scroll down to the last page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those signatories members of the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those individuals that you had spoken with?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: How do you mean "spoke with"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived in early September and during those first several days of September, did you speak with those individuals?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me what this report appears to be.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I've seen the heading and the bottom. I guess it's a report by the inspection team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in the drafting of this document?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the first page, is your participation on the inspection team discussed in this document?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In this report you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no. I mean, I didn't read it. I don't know. On page 4, my name is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever sent a copy of this report?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Oh, just one more question: Is there any information in this report concerning the killing of civilians in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't read it and I did not participate in the drafting of this report, and my name is not among the signatories at the bottom of the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. Sir, let's return to September 29th. You've testified that you had drafted a report and sent it in to Sarajevo and that you didn't file any other reports after this one. How long did you remain in Jablanica after filing that last report, the one with the names of the villages from Grabovica, the 30 names? How long did you remain in Jablanica after filing that report?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed for a few more days. I don't know exactly how many. And since I was there alone, I didn't have any orders from Sarajevo to come back. I stayed there for a few days. And then when I saw that I wasn't getting any orders, and I saw also that all the units were returned to Sarajevo because the action to unblock Mostar was finished, I at my own initiative organised my own trip back and returned to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to returning to Sarajevo while you were in Jablanica, was any proper investigation of the killings in Grabovica ever conducted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's on objection to that question. The comment "was a proper investigation done" is one of those comments, rather than questions. There'll be a closing speech. There's a time for that to be said, but it's not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that without that word "proper" your question could still stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an investigation conducted?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know what I did. As for the rest, I don't know if anybody from amongst the army members carried out an investigation. I didn't see anybody. I didn't meet or contact anybody. I didn't receive any assistance in what I was doing either. I did what I could, and I informed my superiors in Sarajevo about all the things that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Jablanica, did anyone ever ask you for a status report as to the murders in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After returning to Sarajevo, did anyone ever ask you for a status report concerning the murders in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the word "status."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A report as to what's happening.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Other than the reports that I sent then, when I was there, nobody ever asked me for any other kind of report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to Sarajevo, did anyone from the inspection team ever contact you in relation to the murders in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever offer assistance in relation to the murders in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that's the third time we've had that very same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you returned to Sarajevo, did you ever go back to Grabovica for any reason in relation to those murders?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon your return to Sarajevo, did you speak with anyone concerning Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No one asked me any specific questions about it. I reported to the security administration then, and nobody ever asked me any specific questions about it. All I know is that within the scope of the Trebevic operation, as the members of the 9th and 10th, some of them, that is, were involved in that operation, we were told to interview them in connection with Grabovica, those who had been there at the time. I did not have occasion to speak to any of the soldiers who had been in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since you mentioned Operation Trebevic, when did you first learn about that operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't find out about it specifically. On my return from Jablanica, Mr. Jasarevic gave me about ten days to go home and have a rest, because I hadn't been in Sarajevo for several months. So I went home. And the beginning of Operation Trebevic found me at home. I saw that something was going on in town, that everything was blocked, so then I got ready and went to the security administration. That's when I heard that the Operation Trebevic I was underway. I had never heard about it before, and I had not participated in the preparations. I didn't know that this operation was about to begin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the security administration, did you find out or did you learn what the goal of Operation Trebevic was?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I was told that Operation Trebevic I was underway and that its goal was for parts of the units on the territory of Sarajevo who were not under control and who did not respect the hierarchy and discipline, for matters to be cleared up with these individuals and groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Operation Trebevic concerned crimes in what area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just interrupt the witness. Witness, pardon me. It's an objection to the question, not the answer. The witness's evidence didn't use the word "crimes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The witness said it was discipline measures or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Operation Trebevic concerned problems in what area?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, failure to respect -- although I'm not an expert to use expert terminology, to respect command and control, to respect orders from the corps, lack of discipline, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But where were these failures occurring?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand "where." Do you mean in terms of location or do you mean in what units?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, in what location?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, what units were involved or what units were targeted during this Operation Trebevic I?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The object of Operation Trebevic I was for the most part to focus on units of the 9th and 10th Brigades; however, there were also cases in other units in Sarajevo where there were soldiers who were not part of the system, so to say, and there were remnants of Juka Prazina's units, and this covered the entire area of Sarajevo. The main focus was on problems in the 9th and 10th Brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you given any assignments when you went to the security administration building in relation to Operation Trebevic I?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I interviewed members of the 9th and 10th Brigades, and this took place in the building on the premises of the security services administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you given any assignments or duties as to what areas to question these people about?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Every morning we had a meeting, the members of the security administration, and the meeting was also attended by security men from the corps and from the brigades who were there to assist because of the large number of men to be interviewed. We received instructions that we were to interview the men in connection with what I've just mentioned, lack of obedience and so on, things that were illegal, so to say, that happened in the brigades and that were done by the soldiers. The orders were also that those soldiers who had been in the area of Grabovica at the time were also to be interviewed in connection with the murders in Grabovica and statements were to be taken in connection with these events also, but I myself was not assigned, because it was our superiors who assigned interviewees to us, and I was not assigned any soldier to interview who had been in Grabovica at the time of the events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after Operation Trebevic, did you ever issue -- or did you ever write any reports in relation to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive inquiries from anyone, from the inspection team or anyone else in relation to Grabovica, after the Trebevic operation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, maybe we could have a break and -- so that to keep the cross-examination in a whole piece. Well, we'll have 30 minutes' break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dzankovic. Mr. Dzankovic, I just want to go chronologically, if possible, at the moment and commence with a couple of questions about your experience, which the Prosecution asked you about. You had some firsthand experience in the actual fighting early on in the war at a place called Kuc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: A place called ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I -- I'm sorry, I mispronounced it. Zuc. Zuc or Zuk.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Zuc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you feel free to correct the pronunciation of an Australian member of counsel, please, Mr. Dzankovic. I'll do my best. In any event, when you were fighting there, you came to know something about the way in which the fighting units were -- the way in which the fighting units were born. And what I wanted to ask you is this: Did you observe a lot of the units in the Bosnian army to be spontaneously created units?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course they were spontaneously created units. We were waging a war of liberation against an army that we ourselves helped to create, but we did not have an army of our own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that at that time you were operating at the level of a fighter and you weren't a member of the General Staff, but just from your own experience, what did you observe about the creation of local units in Sarajevo and in particular, how did they choose their commanders?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of the war, we were self-organised. We gathered together from various parts of town and we organised ourselves and armed ourselves in every possible way. We even used drainage pipes and nails to create weapons. We had no organisation as such. After that, we set out to organise something that was called the Territorial Defence. These were in fact the reserve forces of the former JNA, and it was on the basis of this that units began to be formed, which were then given specific tasks. Before that, we ran from every part of town to where we were most needed. Wherever we heard that there was combat activity going on, we all ran to that place in order to stop the aggressors from penetrating into the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- thank you for that. And you came to know while you were fighting that Sefer Halilovic was the head man of the army carrying at that time the title of Chief of Staff of the Main Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in those days, Sefer Halilovic was a popular figure within the citizens -- among the citizens of Sarajevo because he was leading the struggle for the resistance against the -- the enemy.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not only at the beginning, but also later, later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And under the leadership of -- of Sefer Halilovic, the Main Staff of the army bit by bit tried to bring in rules to transform the spontaneous units into a functioning army; is that an accurate comment?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I right -- this is a comment of mine, but I'd ask you to make -- give your comments, because you were there. Is it a fair comment to make that in about September 1993, when these sad events happened, the Bosnian army was becoming more organised but was still very much a work in progress?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in particular, in August and September of 1993, what -- the army and -- well, I won't ask you about other organisations. One of the issues facing the army in August and September of 1993 was to bring units within the proper command and control system; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made reference to some elements of the 9th and 10th Brigades who were not cooperative with that system. And again, I'll just ask for your comment about this: Did it appear that the 9th and 10th -- sorry, I'll take it one step at a time. As to the 9th Brigade -- perhaps I'm going to take another step back. In August and September, had you been in Sarajevo for a while or had you been on the terrain in other places?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The first time I left Sarajevo was when Igman was falling. I didn't leave Sarajevo before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've had some evidence from various witnesses in this case about Igman, and I wonder, just so that the Tribunal can know the time frame of the Igman troubles: When did the battle for Igman start and approximately when did the situation stabilise?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. As far as I can recall this was in June and July, in that period. And there was fighting up there for some 20 days, until we stopped that and set up some sort of lines in order to prevent the aggressors for penetrating into Hrasnica and further on into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So is it accurate to say that in perhaps June and July of 1993 there was trouble on Igman and towards the end of July or around the end of July the Igman troubles stabilised and the front line was fixed? Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we can say that they stabilised, in quotation marks, because there was still fighting going on up there but the situation was kept under control. We no longer allowed the aggressors to advance any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Part of the reason I was asking you that is I'd started to ask you about your knowledge of the -- of certain units in Sarajevo. But is the position this: That you went on to Igman in that time, and after that you went down to Herzegovina? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't go back to Sarajevo from Igman. I went right on to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, did you have a -- perhaps I -- I just want to take -- there's a couple of preliminary questions before we get into the Herzegovina situation. The first one is this: You indicated to my learned friend the Prosecutor that you had joined the SVB in or about February of 1993. Was that at a time when you were connected to a unit called the 6th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the 6th Mountain Brigade was dissolved, I received an order that I was to report to the security administration at the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. And I'll come to that in a moment. At the time when you were at the 6th Mountain Brigade, did you know an individual named Dzevad Tirak?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was the assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the same Dzevad Tirak who came to be an official within the organisation of the 6th Corps, when that corps was created, in about June 1993?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, within the organisation of the -- the SVB, the security administration, initially when you joined, the head of that organisation was Fikret Muslimovic and his deputy was Jusuf Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you come to report to a man called Vahid Bogunic in that time? When I say "report to," was he your immediate superior in Sarajevo, in terms of the professional line of reporting?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: When I received the order to report to the security administration, the first interview with me was conducted by Mr. Fikret Muslimovic. And after interviewing me for some 10 or 15 minutes, he said I was to report to Mr. Vahid Bogunic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And up until the time you went on to Igman, was Vahid Bogunic the person with whom you dealt most frequently from the UB?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And just so that -- just to refresh the Tribunal's memory, the UB is the senior level of the SVB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, I'm asking you because -- yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, sometimes I have to put a proposition to you to clarify it for us in this Tribunal. Very well. Thank you. Now, the next question I have for you is that when you went out onto Igman, was part of your job to perform operative work there to find out what had gone wrong on Igman? Perhaps I'll take a step back from that. The battle for Igman involved a -- a large retreat by Bosnian army forces, didn't it, which ended up being stabilised at the end of that particular battle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Rogoj fell near Trnovo, the army started withdrawing, retreating before the aggressor's attacks, and it was in a state of dissolution until at Igman we finally managed to establish the lines and stop the enemy advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And was part of your task when you were send onto the terrain at Igman to investigate what had gone wrong and to propose -- well, perhaps I'll ask you that part first. First of all, was it to investigate what had gone wrong?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the spot, in the trenches I spoke to the men. And then I went down to Hrasnica and drew up reports and sent them on to the security administration in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Now, after that time, did you receive an order to go onto the terrain down at -- in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to show you an order now and see if you -- if you recognise that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could the witness please be shown 65 ter number D450, and its number is DD002077, and it's to be MFI282.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's going to be brought up now is an order. And I just want you see if you've seen it before and if you recognise it. Just watch that screen. Okay. Now, there's a document on the screen before you. Would you just take the opportunity to read that briefly and check the bottom and the top of it. While you're doing that, I make the point to you that I'm going to show you a number of documents here. You may never have seen some of them. You may have forgotten some others. And it's up to you to tell us what the situation is about that. Now, with respect to this document here, have you had a chance to look at that briefly?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have not seen this document before. In Hrasnica, I was told orally that I was to go to Herzegovina. It was only later in my conversations with the investigators of The Hague Tribunal that I was shown this document. I have never had it in my hands before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand. But having regard to that document, was it your understanding that you had been dispatched under the authority of Rasim Delic to perform the tasks which are set out -- well, sorry, it doesn't really specify the task awfully well. But was it your understanding that there was -- even though you didn't see it, that there was an order in existence which required the -- the SVB units in the areas of the 4th and 6th Corps to receive you and to help you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: According to what it says here, that's how it should have been. In fact, before I went to Igman, on one occasion I spoke with Jusuf Jasarevic and Vahid Bogunic, and then they intimated to me that there was a possibility for me to be sent to that area for the simple reason that no one had ever visited these corps from the security administration. And I was told that in my conversations with them I should see what the problems were and to inform the command -- or rather, the security administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. So effectively you were being sent down in your professional capacity as an SVB operative in order to gather information and to report back on the security organs of the 4th and 6th Corps; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not the 6th Corps but the security administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, pardon me. That's -- that was what I meant, and I apologise. But -- so the security administration of the 6th Corps and of the 4th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to be clear what the status of this -- this document here is before I decide whether to offer it for tender or not. This document, you've never seen. But to your knowledge, did your superiors send an order out to smooth your passage and to guarantee that the units down in Herzegovina did cooperate with you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about this order when I was there. The fact is that the 6th Corps and the 4th Corps provided assistance to me. Actually, the 6th Corps was the corps that was in Konjic, and they helped me to get to Jablanica, and then from Jablanica I went to Mostar on foot, and that's where I stayed the longest. I only spent the night in Konjic and then continued on my way. Once I got there, I was there for a few days. Maybe seven days. I don't know exactly. And I had talks there. I went to the security administration of the 4th Corps and I even sent some reports to Sarajevo from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Okay. Well, now, did you come to know Nermin Eminovic when you passed through the area of the 6th Corps, he being the head of security in the 6th Corps at that time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have the opportunity to get in touch with Mr. Eminovic. When I was there, I was in contact with Mr. Braco Fazlic. His nickname is Braco, but I think his first name is Behudin. He was the chief of the 6th Mountain Brigade staff and he was also the Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. He was not a member of your professional organisation, the SVB, was he?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Okay. Now, you then proceeded on to Mostar. Was it in Mostar that you came to know Sejo Brankovic or did you know him previously or did you meet him for the first time in Jablanica later on?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I met Mr. Sejo Brankovic in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Was that on the way down to Mostar, or after you returned back from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: First I met him in Jablanica and spent a couple of hours with him on my way to Mostar. On my way back, since he was also staying at the same hotel as me, we established contact again, and that's when the cooperation started, which was then continued later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. I understand that. Now, just excuse me a moment, please. All right. Were you ever shown a copy of the order creating the -- the inspection team which you -- of which you were a part? I don't mean during the course of this ICTY investigation. I mean at the time. Did anyone show you a copy of the order?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's another document that I now wish to show the witness. This is Defence 65 ter number D643. It's got an A and a B. And I'll just -- could we just, please, show DD002128. And that's to be MFI283.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this order is an order coming from Jusuf Jasarevic and asking that you be found and asking that you report to Sefer Halilovic. I'm going to take you through that order in just a moment. Do you have a copy of that order on the screen yet?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall when you were down in Mostar receiving a summons to go and meet with -- sorry, that was telling you to "immediately report to the command post of the 6th Corps, to the Supreme Command Staff team headed by Sefer Halilovic, Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, where he will be representing security administration in the team," and by that I think it means you will be representing security administration in the team. Were you given such an order?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received this order and acted in accordance with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And your understanding was when you received the order that you would be representing the security administration in that team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It is admitted into the evidence with the MFI number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit 283.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you've indicated that upon receipt of that order, you then walked across the difficult mountain path from the Mostar area, arriving in Jablanica about 18 hours later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've -- you've been asked a lot of questions by my learned friend Mr. Weiner, and I'm certainly not going to take you through all of those matters again. I -- there's a couple of matters I do wish to cover with you, however. When you first arrived in -- at Donja Jablanica, you arrived at the very tail end of a meeting of that inspection team at which Sefer Halilovic himself was present and also Messrs. Suljevic, Karic, and Bilajac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived. They were already in the room where I was brought in by the soldiers. They were sitting there and talking. I really don't know when this meeting started. I don't know whether it was the beginning or the end of it. In any case, I came into the room and they were all there, and I greeted them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. And you've indicated that from that time -- from that time on, you -- you only attended one actual meeting of this team, in terms of military preparations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you went to the -- now, there was a -- there was an office which you were calling an IKM at the hydroelectric offices in Jablanica. And you personally attended at the IKM on more than one occasion; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went there on several occasions, but not for meetings which related to operations when the unit commanders were there from the 6th Corps, those who were there and -- I did go there, but I actually went there every morning. And if I met any of the inspection team members, I would spend some time with them. However, official meetings where combat activities were discussed were something that I did not attend, except for the one that I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. There was an occasion when you went with team members up to Buturovic Polje, but on that occasion you didn't attend the meeting that was held there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. All right. Well, I want to now turn to the meeting that you -- that you did attend. This was a meeting that had as its focus the provision of logistics to the units that were going to arrive in Jablanica on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was a meeting that, in fact, did take place at the IKM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And present at that meeting were Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, the Minister for the Interior, Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The War Presidency president -- does the name Safet Cibo assist your memory?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard of him, but he wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah. The person -- you mentioned that there was another person present. I must say I had a guess at -- not a guess, but I put Cibo to you. Was this person that was present a local official?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a civilian, the head of the Jablanica municipality. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to be clear as to Mr. Cibo. Is the position this, that it definitely wasn't him, or you don't know whether it was him or not?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't Safet Cibo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Thank you. All right. Now, as -- to your knowledge, Sefer Halilovic was -- was absent up in the Konjic area on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he wasn't in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Anyway, during the course of this meeting, did Vehbija Karic announce that in fact the units from Sarajevo had arrived in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it, in fact, in that context that the discussion about supplies took place? In other words, we've got to feed these troops because they've arrived from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the units that were there in that area had their own logistics and had the accommodation and food problems resolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And although I understand you didn't take a direct part in -- in the original planning of that, to your knowledge -- to your understanding, Zuka's unit was going to assist the arriving troops from Sarajevo with accommodation and with logistics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it that way. The food for those units was discussed during their stay in the Grabovica region. I remember that the chief of the municipality and Mr. Kovacevic actually got the tasks to secure food for the units which had come from, let's say, outside, from Sarajevo, although there were also Cedo's Wolves, Handzar Divizija and so on, which were not from Sarajevo, so all the fighters who had come from outside. In the meantime there was also talk that the Lastes had come. All these troops needed to have food and accommodation provided for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And to your knowledge, were the Lastes a civilian -- sorry, were the Lastes a -- a military unit directly under the control of the Minister for the Interior, Bakir Alispahic? And administratively speaking, under the Ministry of the Interior, rather than the army?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was not part of the army. It was a unit comprising police officers and it was directly under the command of Mr. Alispahic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was food for the Laste unit discussed at this meeting, or had the Laste unit already departed in the Mostar direction?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was discussed where this group should be accommodated; however, later it left for Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "later," do you mean later on that day?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Whether it was on the same day or the next morning, I don't know, but they left without telling anything about it in advance, because we from the inspection team actually found out about it once they had already left the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was their departure a surprise, given that they -- well, perhaps I should ask you the foundational question first. Was it expected that the Laste would take place -- would take part in the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it a great surprise when they vanished?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which direction did they go when they left?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did they do that on foot?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when was the last time on that day, the 8th of September, that you saw -- sorry, well, on the day of the arrival of the troops. When was the last time on that day that you saw Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see Mr. Alispahic at all after that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it your movements were, as you described to the learned Prosecutor, that you then went out to Donja Jablanica and picked up some food containers and proceeded on to Grabovica in the -- in the two vehicles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to be quite clear about this, Sefer Halilovic was not with you on that trip to Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just have a couple of questions about what happened out there at Grabovica. Firstly, the times at which you were out there. I take it it was mid-afternoon to late afternoon. So is the time range there: Approximately 2.30 until 3.00, when you arrived, and departing at around 4.00 to 5.00, somewhere in that range? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand. Now, you've indicated already that you had some friends from the -- from the 2nd Independent Battalion to whom you spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I just ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 3, P3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a panoramic photograph that I'm going to show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Actually, I'm sorry, I've made a mistake about that. It's P7. My apologies. I retract that request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were shown this photograph earlier on, and you marked the -- the place where you -- where you stopped. I'm just going to get you to build on that a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be assisted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you already put a mark on the other photograph where it was that you stayed talking to your friends, and I wonder if you wouldn't mind just doing that again on this photograph here.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. Would you mind just marking that with a "1" inside the circle.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to get you to mark a few more things. Could you just explain to the Tribunal: Was that building there that you've indicated, was that fit for habitation, or not?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And while you were there, did you see any signs of -- of soldiers trying to inhabit that house?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. At the time when we arrived, the soldiers were tired. And from what I could see, there was no set place where they were supposed to go. There was no plan. They were just lying on the lawns and wherever they could on their blankets. I remember that there were some men from the 9th and 10th there. There were several of them. They were sitting around. Some of them had gone down to the river to try to catch some fish because we in Sarajevo hadn't seen any meat for years, so they went down there to try to find something to eat. They were quite exhausted because of the long trip from Sarajevo to Jablanica going through Igman and so on. There were some among them who were sleeping on sleeping bags or blankets around the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. You indicated to my learned friend Mr. Weiner that you'd seen a lady speaking to -- or that you spoke to a lady, in fact, who indicated that the soldiers she was dealing with were nice and -- and so on. Can you indicate on that picture there whereabouts this woman was when you spoke to her.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you mind just marking that with a number "2", please.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks very much. Very well. Now, I just wanted to ask you a question about those people from the 10th Brigade that you saw. To your knowledge, the 10th Brigade were -- or those units of the 10th Brigade that came down to -- to Herzegovina, at least, were actually billeted to sleep in the township of Jablanica itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you can say -- did you see three or four soldiers from the 10th Brigade in Jablanica -- in -- in Grabovica when you went there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: In Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, that's what I'm -- you mentioned before -- I may have misunderstood you, but I just want to make sure we -- we understand each other here. You mentioned that you saw some soldiers from the 9th and 10th in the village. Now, can I just ask you this: How do you know that there was any from the 10th there at all at the time when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I said from the 9th or the 10th brigade, because I found out that these units were there in the area. I specifically didn't know who was from which unit. I knew a couple of the guys there who were my friends from the -- a unit of the 1st Independent Battalion. The place where they were sitting, that's where the members of the unit were. I couldn't really specifically say who was from which unit, and that's why I said "from the 9th or the 10th." They were all mixed up together. We didn't have any insignia on our military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. The reason I asked you the question is because the interpretation earlier on had you saying that you saw units from the 9th and the 10th, but what you say now, to clarify that, is that you saw soldiers and they could have been either from the 9th or the 10th and you don't know; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what he said. That's not what he said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness's answer is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I did quote him correctly. But if my learned friend wants to point to another part of the transcript, I'm very happy to put that to him as well. I don't want to be sneaky about it in any way. But I understood that was what -- what was said, and certainly that's what was said just a minute ago. So perhaps -- I'll just proceed with the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, he said, "I said from the 9th or [Realtime transcript read in error "and"] the 10th because I found out that that -- that these units were there in the area."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My friend has just ignored the word "or."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what the controversy is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- I'm not -- I'm not saying that it wasn't 9th or 10th. This witness had indicated these -- that he had heard people from the 9th or 10th were there and he saw a large number of people. He doesn't know other -- everybody in that area other than the two or three friends he had in the 2nd Independent Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the witness himself is the author of the word he said, you know. Maybe you can re-ask this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just forgive me for asking the questions as I have, Witness. I'll -- I'll just ask it again. Well, I'll put it differently. First of all, you saw a large number of soldiers present in Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally do not know if a single one of those soldiers was from the 10th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who was there from the 10th and who was there from the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, but I've got a further question. You are not saying to this Tribunal, are you, that there was anyone there from the 10th at the time when you were present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is your position this: You do not know whether or not soldiers from the 10th were present?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell who was from which brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand that. But what I'm putting to you is it's quite possible that there was no one from the 10th Brigade there on that occasion at all. Do you agree with --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. You're asking him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, yes. That's a step further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that it is. Your Honour, I don't want to debate with Your Honour about it. But if the Prosecutor -- well, I won't -- I won't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you again: As to the units who were there, you knew that -- that there were people from the 2nd Independent Battalion present. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you didn't recognise any soldier from the 10th Brigade present, did you?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nobody pointed out -- well, sorry, when you say "yes" there, now I'm going to have to qualify that. This is not your fault, Witness. Let me assure you. These -- it's the questions and not the answers that are the problems. I just want to be clear about the 10th Brigade. As far as the 10th Brigade, your position is maybe there was and maybe there wasn't. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, we're into speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. No, I don't think so. I think that's a correct reflection of the answer of this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, was your answer to that question yes?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies for the clumsy questions in that instance. Now, let's proceed. Okay. Thank you. Now, as far as you could see in the village, the relations between soldiers and civilians were completely correct and, in fact, relatively friendly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say they were idyllic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers appeared to you to be very relieved and relaxed at getting out of the strict confines of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they were relieved to be out of Sarajevo, but they were relaxed. You could see that they were tired, but everything else was all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as far as you could see, there was no soldiers making inappropriate comments about Croats or criticising Croats or showing any hostility whatsoever to people on the basis of being Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No one either criticised or said bad words about the Croats. Everything was ideal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Vehbija Karic was being driven by his own son in that village, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it within your knowledge that Vehbija Karic's wife is in fact Croatian and that his son is half Croatian?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, as to Vehbija Karic himself, you saw no signs of aggression, impatience, or anti-Croat spirit from him during your time in that village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, he was not intolerant or aggressive. I didn't see that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions about -- about transport. The person who -- you mentioned there was two vehicles, and you said the driver of the second vehicle was a person called Soko. If I mention the name Huso Alic, does that assist your memory in any form as to who that driver was?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I had never met this gentleman either before or after. I knew him by his nickname, Soko. Whether this is his real first and last name, I really don't know. I know that he used to be some kind of commander at Igman. Then he went abroad and came back. These are things I learned from rumours that were going round. But I didn't know this gentleman at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's okay. I think I've exhausted my questions on that topic. Just finally, on the picture that you have in front of you, do you see a large house -- a large white house in the bottom left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you remember whether there were any people, whether soldiers or civilians, at that house during the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the house in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I mean the -- the lower left-hand corner, which has two small chimneys.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: The one with the large terrace in front?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were quite a few soldiers in front of that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was it apparent to you whether there was at that stage a local person connected with that house that you met or could see?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't observe any civilians there, because I brought them a food container with pies as well and I left it there, but I didn't notice any civilians nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you've indicated that at a later time you -- you met with a man called Ramiz Delalic, and I just wanted to ask you: During your time in the village here, did you personally notice Ramiz Delalic on any occasion in the village? I mean on this -- on this -- on this visit with Mr. Karic.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see Ramiz Delalic, Celo, there on the spot while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand. Very well. Are you able to indicate -- you see in the top left there's a partially hidden house?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can see two. Which one are you referring to? The one with bricks or the other one in the upper left-hand corner, to the extreme upper left? Which one are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was referring to not the one in the extreme upper left-hand corner. I was referring to the -- the other one, the one maybe an inch or so, maybe two inches in from the left-hand side but still in -- in the top corner with the tile -- tiled reddish roof.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you see -- did you see any civilians or soldiers associated with that house while you were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any civilians there. I did go up to that house, because my friend Zoran Kovacevic was asleep there in the basement, so I went to that house because my other friend, Cupo, told me that Zoka was up there asleep. I left the food in front of the house, where I circled it. I went up there. I found my friend Zoran Kovacevic. I woke him up. And then together we came back to this house where he started eating, and there we continued our conversation. But up there at that house, I didn't see any civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you mind just marking that top house -- sorry, that -- the Zoran Kovacevic -- Zoran Kovacevic house with a "3".

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, the house in the very top left-hand corner, which is right in the corner, did you notice any civilians or soldiers associated with that house?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you, because I didn't go up there. There are quite a few trees. Now, on this photograph, the vegetation is different from what I remember. There were more trees when we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: So that this house up there, I don't even remember whether I saw it or not, whether I saw it behind the vegetation. I don't know if there was anyone billeted there or whether there was anyone living in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. Now, look, I'm going to move to another topic now. And just noting that there's still five minutes of court time to go, I might just move to a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, I tender -- I offer that document for tender. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Defence Exhibit D284.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Look, I'm just going to jump forward now because we've just got a five-minute spell and I'm just going to use that five minutes for something that's confined. At the end of your examination-in-chief with the learned Prosecutor over there, he showed you a report done by the inspection team. Do you remember he showed you that document?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I won't trouble you with showing it to you again. You made no contribution to that document at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. And, in fact, you didn't sign that, nor did you look at that document before it was sent by the inspection team, who signed off on it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: I neither read this document nor participated in writing it, nor did I sign it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. In fact, your reports concerning the -- the investigation into the terrible events at Grabovica were reports that were sent back up the professional line of reporting within the SVB to General -- I'm sorry, not to General but to Jusuf Jasarevic personally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "N/R" means personally for Jusuf Jasarevic, the chief of the security administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. And that really was your obligation, wasn't it, that when -- in a professional matter such as the investigation of the killings at Grabovica, you were obliged, weren't you, by the rules to report to Jusuf Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I did, because that's what I thought I was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And -- and that's what you understood the instruction from Sefer Halilovic to require you to do, to do what you could do in the circumstances and maintain a reporting contact with Jusuf Jasarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood the order issued by the general, and I did everything in my power. I asked for assistance, and in fact my correspondence was directly with the security administration, of which I was a member. I carried out the order issued by the general to the extent I was able to -- or rather, as ordered by the general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
